rule: **Python**: a call to an external capitalized function that is not known to be a class is a direct call to it (`mod.Name`), not `Name#<init>`.
source: KNOWN_GAP: external capitalized functions are guessed to be constructors
notes: Decisions 2026-10-29 (Python): `MakeClient` and `vendorlib.Connect` are external capitalized names not known to be classes -> direct calls `mod.Name`, medium; never `MakeClient#<init>` / `vendorlib.Connect#<init>`. Contrast: a scanned capitalized function `BuildLocal` is a direct high call to its definition, and the scanned class `Local` is a constructor.
